dist.immediate:
No delay — token passes through instantly.
Use for: routers, sorters, immediate branching.
Note: avoid self-loops (P→T→P) — causes livelock.
dist.exp:
Exponential random delay, memoryless.
Use for: arrivals, failures, service times.
E.g. mean=5 → avg 5 s between firings.
dist.norm:
Bell-curve random delay.
Use for: machining, processing with natural spread.
E.g. mean=10, std=2 → usually 8–12 s.
dist.unif:
Flat random in [mean−std, mean+std].
Use for: any delay in a range equally likely.
E.g. mean=10, std=3 → uniform 7–13 s.
dist.det:
Fixed constant delay, same every time.
Use for: conveyors, known fixed durations.
E.g. mean=3 → always exactly 3 s.

hints.meanDelay:
Average time (sim units) the transition holds a token before firing.
→ Exp: mean of the distribution
→ Normal / Uniform: center of the range
→ Det: exact fixed duration
Example: mean=60, scale=seconds → avg 1 min hold time.
hints.stdDeviation:
Spread around the mean. Used by Normal and Uniform only.
→ Normal: ~68% of delays fall in [mean−std, mean+std]
→ Uniform: values drawn uniformly from [mean−std, mean+std]
Set to 0 for Exp or Det (has no effect).
Example: mean=10, std=3 → mostly 7–13 s.
hints.priority:
Firing order when multiple enabled transitions compete for the same token.
Default is 1 (normal). Higher number fires first.
Equal-priority transitions are resolved by probability weights.
Example: T1(priority=2) always fires before T2(priority=1) regardless of probability.
hints.probability:
Firing weight among same-priority transitions that compete from the same place.
Enter 0–100%. Competing transitions must not exceed 100% total.
Any unset transitions share the remaining percent equally.
Leave blank if this transition has no same-priority competitors.
